title: Finite-fibre sheaf quotient with its canonical unit
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes, $F$ an $\mathcal O_X$-module and $y\in Y$. Put $A=\mathcal O_{Y,y}$, $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_A$, $X'=\operatorname{Spec}(A)\times_Y X$, $g:X'\to X$, $F'=g^*F$ and $J=\mathfrak m\mathcal O_{X'}$ [def-pc-fibre-product, def-pc-module-pullback, def-nagata-extended-ideal]. For $n\ge0$ put $X_n=\operatorname{Spec}(A/\mathfrak m^{n+1})\times_Y X$, let $i_n:X_n\to X$ and $j_n:X_n\to X'$ be the canonical maps, and put $F_n=i_n^*F$ [def-weil-pbc-formal-fibre-cohomology, def-weil-pbc-formal-functions-finite-pullback]. Write $q_n:F'\to F'/J^{n+1}F'$ for the quotient projection [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module] and $u_n:F'\to j_{n,*}F_n$ for formalFunctionsFiniteFMap. Then $j_n$ is a closed immersion and there exists an isomorphism $e_n:F'/J^{n+1}F'\cong j_{n,*}F_n$ with $e_n\circ q_n=u_n$. This is a sheaf statement, without cohomology or transition assertions.

proof.text: Unfold the let-bindings and introduce n. Apply the closedness theorem for the canonical finite map, then apply the finite-level quotient transport theorem to obtain the compatible isomorphism.
